drafts.title: Seating ergonomics and reliable memory for tall occupants
drafts.description: Tall drivers and rear passengers experience longer thigh support, competitive rear legroom, and dependable memory recall so they sit comfortably on every trip.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat cushion provides at least 60 mm additional thigh support length versus the current baseline; rear-seat knee clearance (legroom) is >= 975 mm measured at SAE seating reference positions; seat memory restores the saved driver position within ≤2 cm linear displacement and ≤2° angular deviation in ≥98% of restore attempts after vehicle start or door close, across ambient temperatures -10°C to +40°C.
assumptions: Current 5 Series baseline thigh length can be extended by ~60 mm without unacceptable packaging or seatback rake compromises.
975 mm rear knee clearance is approximately equal to or better than main competitors in the midsize luxury segment at successor launch.
Seat actuator and sensor accuracy needed to meet the memory tolerance is implementable within 3–5 years.
uncertainties: Exact competitor rear-legroom figures at launch may differ from our assumption and could require small target adjustments.
Packaging trade-offs with optional equipment (panoramic roof, battery placement) may reduce achievable rear knee clearance in some variants.

drafts.title: Practical storage and trunk power for everyday bottles and portable coolers
drafts.description: Customers can use real-world drink containers in the cabin and power a portable cooler from the trunk without workarounds.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front cup holders securely accept and retain bottles up to 90 mm in diameter and upright 1.5 L bottles without tipping in ≥95% of typical driving maneuvers; trunk includes an accessible 12 V socket capable of delivering continuous 10 A to power portable coolers, usable without disassembling trunk lining.
assumptions: Most commonly used bottles and 1.5 L containers have diameters ≤90 mm.
Typical portable coolers draw ≤10 A continuous; 10 A is sufficient for the majority of customer use cases.
uncertainties: Some specialty coolers or accessories could draw >10 A and would need a higher-current option.
Trunk packaging and optional spare-tire configurations may constrain socket placement.

drafts.title: Exterior access works reliably in cold and everyday conditions (hands‑free tailgate and flush door handles)
drafts.description: Customers can open the tailgate with a single hands-free gesture and use the door handles reliably even after freezing conditions, without repeated attempts or manual intervention.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Hands-free tailgate opens on the first valid foot gesture within ≤2.5 seconds in ≥95% of attempts across ambient temperatures -20°C to +40°C and after light precipitation; flush door handles operate (unlock and open on first user action) in ≥95% of cycles when tested after a 12‑hour exposure at -20°C with surface ice formation.
assumptions: Standardized test protocols for gesture detection and handle operation (timing, number of attempts) will be used in validation.
Environmental tests (freezing with ice formation) represent typical winter conditions experienced by customers in affected markets.
uncertainties: Extreme environmental contamination (salt, thick ice buildup) beyond test conditions may still impair operation.
Some aftermarket covers or waxes applied to surfaces may affect freeze behavior.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with broader color and brightness control
drafts.description: Customers can personalize interior mood lighting with many colors, fine brightness steps and persistent presets.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ambient lighting offers at least 64 distinct color choices, at least 10 discrete brightness levels, and at least 3 user-configurable presets; per-zone lighting settings persist across ignition cycles and apply to front and rear zones independently.
assumptions: 64 colors and 10 brightness levels provide noticeably finer control versus current offering and match customer expectations.
Per-zone persistence is implemented in user profile storage that survives normal vehicle power cycles.
uncertainties: Additional colors and zones may have small impacts on supply chain (LED modules) and software UI complexity.
